text: Which gamepad placement model should BRL-0048 carry into implementation?
suggestions: Use the recommended latched target vector: stick position maps directly to a direction and normalized range, neutral retains the last target, and first use starts around mid-range.
Use a virtual cursor: stick deflection moves the reticle over time and neutral stops it.
Use direction-only placement at a fixed range and give up analog short-to-long distance selection.

text: After handler-level filtering and renormalization, what should a neutral right stick mean for ranged placement?
suggestions: Map normalized magnitude directly to range: neutral is zero/minimum distance and full deflection is maximum distance; retain only the last direction because zero has no angle.
Latch the complete previous target: neutral retains both direction and distance until the stick moves again.

text: Use active-only normalized-vector targeting: a non-neutral right stick supplies direction and distance; neutral supplies no target. Do not latch or synthesize a fixed/default target.
Neutral means no targeting at all: no target, no retained distance, and no reticle/preview.
What should Fire or Confirm do when a range-targeted weapon or ability has no gamepad target?
suggestions: Reject/suppress the target-required action until the stick is non-neutral; keep a targeted ultimate armed and do not spend lobbed-primary ammunition.
Allow the action using a hidden default or previous target even though no reticle is shown.

text: Primary Fire in neutral should auto-target the nearest enemy's current position. Do not calculate target velocity or lead for the expected impact time.
Should neutral auto-targeting apply only to primary Fire, or also when confirming targeted ultimates?
suggestions: Apply it only to primary weapons; targeted ultimates still require manual stick targeting because restorative and placement abilities do not share a sensible nearest-enemy default.
Apply it to primary weapons and every targeted ultimate, always using the nearest eligible enemy position.

text: What should neutral primary Fire do when no eligible visible enemy exists?
suggestions: Reject the attack without spending ammunition or starting cooldown.
Fire along the fighter’s current facing even though no enemy was auto-targeted.

text: Search authoritative effect-eligible targets in priority order: nearest available enemy fighter first, then nearest available shootable thing such as a chest or barrel. If no target exists, fire straight ahead along the player's current direction.
Apply the same viewport-bounded auto-target priority, current-position aim, and facing fallback to targeted ultimates as to primary Fire.
